title: 90-day concentration slate and all-staff brief
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a compact, practical 90-day concentration slate for the entire company plus a short pre-read and run-of-show for the all‑staff briefing. Audience: leadership, ICs across eng/product/gtm, and people ops. Goal: align the org on the next 12 weeks of concentrated work, the measurable OKRs we will use to judge success, and the asks we will make of teams during the all-staff.

Topline executive summary (one paragraph):
We will focus the next 90 days on three cross-cutting outcomes: (1) operationalize predictable inference economics (cost/unit down 12% while meeting latency SLOs), (2) finish the Dedicated capacity MVP and onboard two pilot customers, and (3) neutralize three top reliability risks for Private deployments (networking, KMS integration, and deploy rollback). These will be our company-level priorities and the all-staff will be used to (a) explain why, (b) demonstrate success metrics, and (c) surface team-level commitments.

Company OKR draft (proposed — feedback requested)
Objective A: Make inference economics predictable and 12% cheaper per effective token for common web workloads.
- KR A1: Reduce average per-token compute cost on hosted-api for tail traffic by 12% vs baseline (measured across gen+chat routes). Owner: Priya Kapoor.
- KR A2: Increase prefix/KV cache hit rate on production routes from 18% to 34%. Owner: Eng-serving-runtime (Samir Rao).
- KR A3: Deliver 3 optimizer recommendations (batching, quantization profiles) into Redwood Optimize with automatic suggested bucket. Owner: product-optimize (Diego Martinez).

Objective B: Deliver Redwood Dedicated MVP and validate with two pilot customers.
- KR B1: Complete Dedicated orchestration and autoscaling parity with basic SLOs by end of Q1 (throughput testbench passing). Owner: infra/dedicated (Claire Nguyen).
- KR B2: Sign 2 pilot contracts and complete onboarding runbook end-to-end. Owner: sales-eng (named lead: Anya Patel).
- KR B3: Deliver a canary rollout tooling flow in Console to route 10% traffic to Dedicated variant. Owner: product-console.

Objective C: Harden Private deployments for regulated customers.
- KR C1: Achieve KMS/HSM integration checklist completion + audit run for one pilot. Owner: security-and-compliance.
- KR C2: Reduce average private-deploy recovery time from 45m to <12m for common failures (net/KV/oom). Owner: platform-engineering/SRE.
- KR C3: Publish an on-prem install checklist and a telepresence troubleshooting guide. Owner: solutions-engineering-and-professional-services.

Why these? Short rationale (for the all-staff):
- Economics: customers are making decisions at per-token unit economics; improving cache and batching is high-leverage.
- Dedicated: predictable capacity is the gateway to larger ARPU; need to prove first installations are low-touch and stable.
- Private: regulatory deals unlock enterprise motion; reducing time-to-recover and a clear compliance story removes the top objections.

All-staff pre-read (to be sent 48 hours ahead)
- One-page summary of the 3 objectives and each KR (this doc).
- Two short customer vignettes: a) a startup for whom cost-improvements unlock scale; b) an enterprise asking for Private/Rollout guarantees.
- 90s video (CEO): framing and why concentrated effort matters.
- Link to the interactive dashboard with current baselines: /console/portal/90day-baselines (internal).

All-staff run-of-show (35 minutes total)
- 0–3 min: welcome + cadence reminder (CEO)
- 3–8 min: state-of-play — metrics baseline & constraints (CPO)
- 8–18 min: three priority spotlights (6 min each) — economics, Dedicated, Private. Each spotlight: one slide, two bullets: why it matters, what we will ship in 90 days. Owners present.
- 18–25 min: customer vignette readout + short demo (solutions eng)
- 25–32 min: org asks (clear, time-bound asks to teams). We will call three specific cross-team needs (see below).
- 32–35 min: quick Q&A and next steps (CEO + moderator).

Org asks (specific, timeboxed)
- Engineering: reserve 20% sprint capacity in weeks 1–4 for cache rework + kernel tuning (apply to serving-runtime teams).
- Product/Console: ship the Dedicated routing UI canary toggle by end of week 6 for internal testing.
- Solutions & SRE: prepare two runbook walk-through sessions (30m) for pilot customers in weeks 8–10.

Risks and mitigation (top 6)
- Risk: Dedicated performance regressions in tail cases. Mitigation: testbench gating + automated rollback + perf regressions alerting.
- Risk: Cache changes regress hallucination profiles. Mitigation: QA prompt-eval harness tied to Redwood Optimize.
- Risk: On-prem networking edge cases. Mitigation: create a small lab environment with customer-like NAT/firewall config and a reproducible test matrix.
- Risk: Sales timeline slips. Mitigation: prebuilt onboarding package + internal ‘red-team’ install to validate docs.
- Risk: Org burnout from context switching. Mitigation: focused 90-day timer, limit new large initiatives, weekly health check survey.
- Risk: Exec misalignment. Mitigation: weekly 15m sync between CEO/CPO/VP Eng to keep decisions tight.

Decision points needed before all-staff (owners + due dates)
- Finalize company OKRs and commit to numerical targets (Owner: CEO/CPO) — due: 2025-01-22.
- Decide whether cost target is 12% vs conservative 8% (data ask to infra billing team) — due: 2025-01-20.
- Approve Dedicated pilot customer list and NDA/legal template — due: 2025-01-24.

Measurement and dashboards (what we will show)
- Weekly dashboard: per-token cost trend (hosted-api aggregate), cache hit rate, latency p95 across gen routes. (Priya/observability)
- Dedicated readiness scorecard: orchestration pass/fail, end-to-end latency, burst capacity availability. (Claire)
- Private deploys health: avg recovery time, incident count, audit readiness. (security-and-compliance)

Communications plan post-all-staff
- Day 0 (immediately): publish slides + pre-read link + action tracker in shared drive.
- Day 1–7: team-level kickoff meetings, ask leads to publish sprint-level commitments.
- Weekly: 15m cross-org sync (Tuesday) to unblock top 3 risks.
- Midpoint (45 days): short update to company with progress vs KRs.

Open questions for leadership (to resolve before final OKRs)
- Can we safely reserve 20% sprints across all eng teams for first 4 weeks? (VP Eng decision)
- Is the 12% cost reduction aggressive relative to expected model mix change? (Finance + research)
- Which two customers are highest priority for Dedicated pilots (and who will be the primary PM accountable)?

Appendix: short owner contact list
- CEO: Mark Prescott (mark@redwood.ai)
- CPO: Lina Morales (lina@redwood.ai)
- Head of Infra/Dedicated: Claire Nguyen (claire@redwood.ai)
- Head of Serving Runtime: Samir Rao (samir@redwood.ai)
- Product Optimize: Priya Kapoor (priya@redwood.ai)
- Company Ops (doc owner): Evelyn Zhang (evelyn@redwood.ai)

Quick informal notes (things to consider adding to playbook)
- A three-phrase elevator pitch for the all-staff: why economy + Dedicated + Private unlock the next set of customers.
- One minimal checklist for pilot handoff that sits in GitHub as a template.
- A short pulse survey post-all-staff asking: was the ask clear? do you have the capacity? what blockers exist?

Next steps (immediate)
- Eve to finalize slides and circulate pre-read by 2025-01-20.
- Leadership to approve final OKR numbers by 2025-01-22.
- Product and infra to provide baselines dashboard link by 2025-01-21.

(End of brief)

Notes to self: this draft should feel compact — aim for one actionable metric per KR, avoid overlapping owners, and keep the all-staff ask count to no more than three to minimize follow-through friction.
